decisions.question: flutter-binding@v1's topic widgets read getCurrentValue / getBufferedValues at their T in every build, which bus-api@v1 G41 (amended in S31) now makes throw TypeError for an off-type value published through a widened reference. What does the widget's observed subscription do, and is the outcome node-local or an amend of flutter-binding@v1? (routed from S20.orchestrator and S31)

options.label: typed subscription
options.consequence: The stand-in's form: observe at T, skip first values by count. An off-type first value is skipped by the runtime so the count swallows the next on-type value and the widget stays on its build error (F4a); an off-type later value goes to the provider zone's uncaught handler, failing a testWidgets body, and marks nothing (F4b); a replay widget fails to mount for good (F4c).

options.label: widened subscription, amend G5 and G6
options.consequence: observe<Object?>(topic), first values counted as 1 or getBufferedValues<Object?>.length: no conversion can fail, the off-type value marks a rebuild, the build's read at T throws into Flutter's build error reporting, the next on-type value renders again (F4a to F4c). Consumer-visible, so a compatible amend of G5 and G6.

options.label: catch the TypeError in build
options.consequence: Rendering the last good frame needs the held copy Refinement 5 forbids; rendering nothing hides the error Flutter would report.

decisions.chosen: widened subscription, amend G5 and G6
decisions.why: The experiment shows the typed form leaves a stale error frame after the topic is valid again and leaks the conversion error to the provider zone, while the widened form recovers on the next on-type value and reports the error once, through Flutter, where build errors belong. The subscription carries no value into the build, so its type argument is invisible except for off-type values. App pages can observe the outcome, so it is an amend, compatible because G5 and G6 stated nothing for off-type values and no fixture publishes one.

decisions.question: flutter-binding@v1 G17 says WidgetTestBus.stub returns 'the same writer on every call for topic', the per-type-argument problem bus-testing@v1 G18 and bus-api@v1 G20 had. Amend or node-local? (routed from S20.orchestrator and S31)

options.label: one publisher per topic, writer per type argument, amend G17
options.consequence: One claim per topic as bus-api@v1 G20 allows, a stable writer per type argument (F5), aligned with bus-testing@v1 G18 as amended; consumer-visible, compatible.

options.label: one cached writer cast per type argument
options.consequence: The stand-in's form; throws TypeError on the second type argument (F5).

options.label: a publisher per type argument
options.consequence: A second claim of the topic, rejected by bus-api@v1 G20 with ClaimRejected.

decisions.chosen: one publisher per topic, writer per type argument, amend G17
decisions.why: The current wording cannot hold for a widened call followed by a typed one; the experiment confirms the stand-in throws and the per-type-argument form keeps one claim. nidana.runtime D7 made the same choice for TestBus.stub, so the two widget-test and VM-test helpers stay alike. App widget tests can observe it, so it is an amend; it also states the ClaimRejected outcome bus-testing@v1 G18 states.

decisions.question: How does the package properties test that checks G18 and G19 find the package's pubspec and sources when it runs under fvm flutter test from the workspace root?

options.label: package URI (Isolate.resolvePackageUri)
options.consequence: The form nidana.runtime D9 and nidana.navigation D4 use under fvm dart test; under fvm flutter test it throws UnsupportedError (F3).

options.label: ancestor search for the workspace root
options.consequence: nidana.model D6's rule (the nearest ancestor holding hsdd/contract/); works from the root and from inside the member (F2, F3).

decisions.chosen: ancestor search for the workspace root
decisions.why: The experiment shows the package-URI approach is unsupported in the flutter_tester environment and the ancestor search works under both invocations; the working directory is the root when the gate runs fvm flutter test --no-pub packages/nidana_dart_runtime_flutter.

decisions.question: How is nidana.flutter cut into phases under fp-progression and the PE limit?

options.label: seven phases: declarations; pure core; router; provider and topic widgets; page scope; module observer with widget-test bus; executor and bootstrap
options.consequence: Each phase one PE (320 to 450 lines with tests and docs); a pure band for the router's stack algebra, the path rules and the holder counts; G7 and G10 replay after the router their cases host; G17 replays with the module observer its last case uses.

options.label: six phases, pure helpers folded into effect phases
options.consequence: One cycle fewer, but the stack algebra and holder counts are tested only through widget tests, against the pure band of fp-progression.

options.label: bootstrap (G16) as its own phase
options.consequence: One case and no code of its own; below the sizing floor.

decisions.chosen: seven phases: declarations; pure core; router; provider and topic widgets; page scope; module observer with widget-test bus; executor and bootstrap
decisions.why: The fixture cases dictate the order (G7's and G10's cases host a FlutterNavigationRouter, G17's last case needs a module observer, G16 needs the executor, the module observer and a BusProvider), and the stand-in's 741 lines grow to seven PEs with doc comments and own tests. The page scope and module observer merged would be two PEs, so they stay split and run side by side.

decisions.question: The root types runtime to flutter 'hard' for bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1 and its Development flow starts the node after the runtime ships. Which producer phase does each nidana.flutter phase wait on?

options.label: per phase by need
options.consequence: nidana.flutter.1 waits on nidana.runtime.1, nidana.navigation.1 and nidana.model.5 (declarations); nidana.flutter.2 and .3 construct no bus and wait on nidana.navigation.2 / .4 and nidana.model.6 / .9; .4 to .7 wait on nidana.runtime.14, and .7 on nidana.navigation.6. The router lane and the tooling workspace lane come off the critical path.

options.label: every phase after nidana.runtime.14
options.consequence: The flow's literal reading; no work on declarations a runtime phase might renegotiate, but nidana.flutter.1 to .3 and nidana.tooling.codegen's workspace lane sit on the critical path.

decisions.why: Root D10 defines a hard edge by the consumer's tests needing the producer's behavior; nidana.flutter.1 runs only analysis sets and a properties test, and the router phases' code and replayed cases (G9, G11 to G13) build no bus. nidana.navigation.1 already waits on nidana.runtime.1 the same way. The signal that would favor the literal reading: an hsdd-contract renegotiation of bus-api@v1's or navigation-api@v1's declarations during nidana.runtime's or nidana.navigation's phases.
evidence: root Dependency DAG and Development flow item 3

decisions.question: What does the type-level phase nidana.flutter.1 land for widgets and argument checks?

options.label: declarations with final fields, constructors that assign and copy, everything else throwing
options.consequence: createState and every computing body throw UnimplementedError; PageScope's and ModuleRoutes' argument checks land with the phases delivering G8 and G9; matches the confirmed reject codes and the model and navigation precedents.

options.label: working States and argument checks from the start
options.consequence: Behavior in a gate-only phase whose gate replays no behavior.

decisions.chosen: declarations with final fields, constructors that assign and copy, everything else throwing
decisions.why: Same reading as nidana.model D3 and nidana.navigation D1; the reject codes were confirmed against final-field getters; behavior stays in phases whose gates replay it.

decisions.question: Source layout of nidana_dart_runtime_flutter below its two public libraries.

options.label: one library per area, pure core under lib/src/core/
options.consequence: Side-by-side phases (.2/.3 against .4, .5 against .6) edit disjoint files, so no Collides with; the pure core imports no Flutter library.

options.label: one library with part files
options.consequence: Every phase edits one library and side-by-side phases serialize.

decisions.chosen: one library per area, pure core under lib/src/core/
decisions.why: Keeps the parallel lanes free of textual contention and the pure band testable without a widget tree; the same choice nidana.navigation D2 made.

decisions.question: What does each gate replay of flutter-binding@v1?

options.label: surface and reject at .1; behavior restricted to the phase's own dependency closure; unrestricted at .7
options.consequence: No gate depends on the merge order of side-by-side phases; the executor binding admits no case until .7 and passes with none run; .7 runs both bindings whole.

options.label: restriction cumulative by phase number
options.consequence: A gate of .4 would replay G9 and G11 to G13, which .4 does not depend on, and fail if .2 or .3 merged later.

decisions.chosen: surface and reject at .1; behavior restricted to the phase's own dependency closure; unrestricted at .7
decisions.why: ADR-001 item 10 restricts to what has been delivered; reading 'delivered' as the dependency closure is the navigation and model precedent for side-by-side phases, and the replay tool passes a binding whose restriction admits nothing.

decisions.question: How do pathOf and PageScope recognize a router route (a route a FlutterNavigationRouter built for one of its entries)?

options.label: identity registry (Expando keyed by the built route)
options.consequence: Exact per the contract's Terms; a package-level weak map.

options.label: settings.arguments is NavigationEntry
options.consequence: No state, as the stand-in did, but misreads a foreign route the app builds with an entry as its arguments.

decisions.chosen: identity registry (Expando keyed by the built route)
decisions.why: Matches the Terms definition exactly; both readings agree for every route a router builds (G13 makes its settings carry the entry), so the choice is invisible across the boundary and stays node-local.

decisions.question: When forwardPlatformRoutes is true, FlutterNavigationExecutor needs WidgetsBinding.instance at construction. Does it initialize the binding itself?

options.label: require the app's bootstrap to initialize it
options.consequence: The executor reads WidgetsBinding.instance before claiming anything, so a missing binding throws with nothing claimed (G14); the app calls ensureInitialized first, as the contract's example does.

options.label: call WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized() itself
options.consequence: Works without app wiring but makes a library decide the app's binding, a global side effect.

decisions.chosen: require the app's bootstrap to initialize it
decisions.why: Initializing the binding is the app's bootstrap decision (the contract's How an app uses it and Guide §3.5's order); only bootstrap misuse can observe the difference, so it stays in nidana.flutter.7's Scope rather than an amend.
evidence: flutter-binding@v1 How an app uses it, G14, G15

decisions.question: Review tier of nidana.flutter.4 (bus provider and topic widgets).

options.label: full-review
options.consequence: Diff read and verification run for the first-value rule, rebuild coalescing, resubscription and shutdown ordering.

options.label: spot-check
options.consequence: Cheaper; G3 to G6 are well constrained by thirteen cases.

decisions.why: The first frame from getCurrentValue without rendering the replayed first value twice is the adapter's core UI property (Refinement 5), and D7's off-type handling is new behavior with no fixture case yet. The signal that would have made it spot-check: an off-type case already in the fixtures.

decisions.question: G8 says a PageScope binds once, at mount. What happens when the enclosing BusProvider starts providing another bus?

options.label: keep the binding, amend G8
options.consequence: The scope stays bound to the bus it mounted under until it unmounts; apps that replace the bus remount pages (key the subtree by the bus).

options.label: rebind to the new bus
options.consequence: Pages follow a replaced bus, but activation and claims run inside didChangeDependencies with failure paths G8 does not state.

decisions.why: G8's 'binds once' reads that way, and ModuleScopeObserver and FlutterNavigationExecutor also hold the bus they were built over; Spec §11.2 recommends against replacing the bus. Consumers can observe it, so it is stated as a compatible amend. Signal for the other option: an adopter that recreates the bus under mounted pages and wants them to follow.

decisions.question: G7 derives an unnamed PageScope's route from settings.name without its leading '/'. For a route named '/', Flutter's default route and WidgetsApp's home route, that is the empty string, which topic-model@v1's PageSource assertion rejects. What is the page source?

options.label: '/' gives PageSource('/'), amend G7
options.consequence: A home page of a named-route app mounts without an explicit route; its source is page:/.

options.label: '/' counts as no route
options.consequence: The stand-in's reading: mounting throws StateError and the app passes route: explicitly.

decisions.why: The rule as written has no conforming outcome for the most common route of a named-route app; naming the root route as the platform names it is a faithful derivation and costs apps nothing. Close call: the signal that would favor the other option is a Guide or Specification convention that page sources never carry a leading slash.

experiments.question: F1/F2: do fvm dart pub get --enforce-lockfile and fvm flutter test --no-pub packages/{member} work from a pure-Dart workspace root with a Flutter member? F3: what does a package test see under fvm flutter test (cwd, Isolate.resolvePackageUri)? F4: what do the topic widgets do with an off-type value under bus-api@v1 G41 as amended, typed against widened subscription? F5: does WidgetTestBus.stub survive one topic at two type arguments?
experiments.finding: F1: both resolution commands exit 0. F2: the member's tests run from the root by path (member dir or its test dir) with the root as working directory. F3: Isolate.resolvePackageUri throws UnsupportedError under fvm flutter test; an ancestor search finds the workspace root. F4: the typed subscription leaves a stale ErrorWidget after an on-type value (F4a), sends the conversion TypeError to the provider zone and marks nothing (F4b), and fails a replay widget's mount for good (F4c); the widened subscription has zero provider-zone errors, reports the build TypeError through Flutter and renders the next on-type value in all three. F5: the stand-in's stub<int> after stub<Object?> throws TypeError; one publisher per topic with writer<T> keeps one claim and a stable writer per type argument.
